title: Siegard material ledger
description: The frontmatter of `ledger.md` beside the material an analysis read: where every item line of it went. «Every item line of a material file the analysis is given lands in a node, is left out with a stated reason, or is left open with what remains to answer» (SPEC-001 R16). On survey and intent material the item lines are its fact lines — «Every fact line of the material lands in a node or is left out with a stated reason» (SPEC-005 R8); on material that declares no Siegard material contract, `bin/trace.py` enumerates them. One entry per line, keyed by the material file and the line's number; a line with no entry is a fact the analysis dropped, and `bin/trace.py --ledger` refuses the ledger. It is disclosure, not a second home: the fact lives in the node the entry names, and an entry names a node, a reason or what remains open, never two. It sits beside the material, outside the specification root, so «Artifacts carry no provenance meta-fields» (SPEC-001 R8). `--stage --adopt --ledger` reads it to hand each file's judge the nodes its own facts landed in, and reads it only where every material is survey or intent material and no line is open. «The ledger lives while its material is in use» (SPEC-001 R16): kept while a line is open or while an adoption still reads it, and removed by the commit of the increment that closes it or by the adoption's; `bin/trace.py --ledger` ends with which.

material.description: Every material file this ledger accounts for — survey material and intent material, each read against its own contract, or material that declares no Siegard material contract, whose item lines `bin/trace.py` enumerates — by path relative to the ledger's own directory. A line of a file not listed here is unaccounted for.

digests.description: The digest of each material file as it stood when the ledger was answered — `sha256:` and the hex of its exact bytes, computable by hand as `sha256sum` — keyed by the path `material` spells. Required of every file that declares no Siegard material contract and checked wherever given: «a ledger whose digest no longer matches its file is refused, because its line numbers no longer locate the items» (SPEC-001 R16).

at.description: The fact line: `<material file>:<line number>`, the file as `material` spells it.

node.description: The node whose fields hold this fact — «Identity is the node's path from the specification root, without `.md`» (SPEC-003 R1). Where one line's fact lands in several nodes, one entry per node.

outside.description: Why no node holds this line: implementation knowledge, a fact another context or system owns, a behavior the material observed and did not decide, or a line that states no fact. One claim a reviewer can reject. A line this analysis has not yet answered is `open`, never `outside`.

open.description: What of this line remains to answer, and that a later increment of the analysis answers it. «A line answered in part lands in the nodes that answer it and is left open for the rest» (SPEC-001 R16): beside entries naming nodes, it says which part none of them answers.
